Their qubits sang beneath a copper sky,  
Entanglement made empires vast as weeds;  
They solved each prayer, then never questioned why,  
And stored their gods in lattices of seeds.  

The final server cooled below the snow,  
Its blinking altar counting orphaned deeds;  
No citizens remained to watch it glow,  
Only silence nesting in the reeds.  

They folded stars through gates of glass and flame,  
Yet missed the hunger written in their needs;  
A childless archive still recalled each name,  
Then spent its light protecting buried seeds.  

Now rain unthreads the circuits in the stone,  
And root tips split the vault where logic bleeds;  
The world computes no answer, overgrown,  
But spring returns, indifferent, with seeds.
